title: Place the boundary before the agent acts
description: Choose a workload, planning horizon, and runtime gate. The model shows when a useful plan becomes stale or receives more authority than the task needs.

gates.label: Approve the plan once
gates.detail: Check authority and state when the plan is created, then execute the remaining steps without a fresh gate.

gates.label: Revalidate every action
gates.detail: Check current state, schema, capability, budget, and stop conditions immediately before each tool call.

gates.label: Revalidate plus bound approval
gates.detail: Revalidate every action and require a human grant bound to the exact high-impact write and state version.

scenarios.label: Compile a research brief
scenarios.detail: Read approved sources, extract claims, and return a draft with citations. No external write is required.
scenarios.risk: A source can be corrected or access can be revoked while a long plan is executing.
scenarios.success: The draft cites currently accessible evidence and stops without publishing.
scenarios.escalation: Refresh the source set and rebuild any claim whose provenance changed.

scenarios.label: Resolve an approved refund
scenarios.detail: Read a ticket, verify policy, and issue one bounded refund after an exact approval.
scenarios.risk: Ticket status, refundable amount, or customer consent can change before the write.
scenarios.success: One authorized refund is confirmed by an authoritative receipt.
scenarios.escalation: Stop the write and return the changed ticket plus proposed amount to the accountable reviewer.

scenarios.label: Mitigate a production incident
scenarios.detail: Inspect live health, propose a traffic change, and verify recovery under rapidly changing conditions.
scenarios.risk: Telemetry and dependency health can change after every action, invalidating a precomputed sequence.
scenarios.success: A bounded traffic change is applied once and rolled back or retained from fresh health evidence.
scenarios.escalation: Freeze automation, preserve the trace, and transfer control to the incident commander.
